abstract: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] Integrating brain imaging data with clinical reports enables the effective use of complementary multimodal information, supporting more accurate and timely diagnosis in real-world clinical settings. This approach has gained growing attention in brain disorder research, yet significant limitations remain: how to encode brain structure and function to reflect meaningful neurological patterns, and how to effectively link objective imaging data with subjective text-based reports while establishing interpretable associations. In this work, we propose a novel multimodal framework that aligns brain connectomes with clinical reports in a shared cross-modal latent space at both subject and connectome levels. Our key innovation lies in treating brain subnetworks as tokens rather than raw image patches, enabling more efficient identification of system-level associations between neuroimaging findings and clinical observations. These cross-modal associations are further fused to enhance mild cognitive impairment (MCI) prediction and provide interpretable diagnostic insights. To our knowledge, this is the first attempt to integrate both structural and functional brain connectivity with non-imaging clinical information. Experimental validation on the ADNI dataset demonstrates performance competitive with recently reported methods. Notably, despite no explicit connectome-token-level supervision, the learned connectome-text associations recover multiple relationships independently reported in the neuroimaging and clinical literature, suggesting that the framework captures clinically coherent cross-modal associations. This pioneering work advances multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis by bridging the gap between neuroimaging analysis and clinical text interpretation through innovative connectome tokenization and cross-modal alignment strategies.

abstract: Predicting clinical trial outcomes requires interpreting biological and clinical evidence in the context of a specific intervention, population and study design. Here we test whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can predict trial outcomes from publicly available evidence. We introduce TrialDossier, which assembles standardized evidence dossiers, and TrialOutlook, which uses these dossiers with GPT-5 to estimate the probability that a trial meets its prespecified primary endpoint. Among 694 ongoing trials with results expected within six months of cohort assembly, 69 outcomes first disclosed after forecast recording had been adjudicated by 20 October 2026. TrialOutlook achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.819 (95% confidence interval, 0.708 to 0.914) and an average precision of 0.860. TrialOutlook correctly identified 27 of 29 failures (93.1%) and incorrectly classified 17 of 40 successes as failures. We further recorded forecasts for 5,809 ongoing trials associated with US-listed companies and established a public benchmark linking archived evidence and fixed forecasts to adjudicated outcomes as they become available.

title: WakeSentry: real-time awakening detection from single-channel EEG across sleep cohorts and forehead headbands
zh_title: WakeSentry：单通道EEG实时觉醒检测
summary: 预印本提出实时觉醒检测模型，在五个睡眠队列1529夜及224个头带夜中外部验证并优于基线。

abstract: Objective/Background: Awakenings after sleep onset are a core measure of sleep continuity, and EEG headbands and closed-loop stimulators, now used at home, must detect each one as it happens, to count it or to stop stimulation. Open sleep stagers match expert scorers, yet have been evaluated only offline over whole nights, so their real-time performance is untested. Patients/Methods: To fill this gap, we developed WakeSentry, which reads only past frontal EEG and learns the moment of waking through an awakening module. We tested it on 1,529 nights from five polysomnography (PSG) cohorts, three clinical, each held out of training, and on 224 headband nights, against GSSC, U-Sleep and YASA. Results: At a matched rate of 0.5 false awakenings per hour, WakeSentry caught more awakenings than GSSC in every cohort and on both headbands. On PSG its sensitivity rose from 63.8% to 70.5%, above U-Sleep and YASA on average. On the headbands it rose from 49.8% to 53.9%, a gain lost without the awakening module. With thresholds preset on the training cohorts, it still outperformed GSSC in six of seven test sets, with at most 0.40 false awakenings per hour. As a replayed stimulator gate, it shortened stimulation during wake in five test sets while staying open for at least 85% of N2 and N3. Conclusions: WakeSentry therefore works in patients and on unseen headbands. It can count awakenings at home and stop stimulation at each one, enabling multi-night monitoring of insomnia and closed-loop stimulation that stops when the sleeper wakes.
zh_abstract: 【目的/背景】睡眠开始后的觉醒是睡眠连续性的核心指标，而如今在家庭中使用的EEG头带和闭环刺激器必须在每次觉醒发生时将其检出，以便计数或停止刺激。开放睡眠分期器与专家评分者表现相当，但仅在整夜数据上进行离线评估，因此其真实时性能尚未经过检验。【患者/方法】为填补这一空白，我们开发了WakeSentry，它仅读取过去的额部EEG，并通过觉醒模块学习觉醒发生的时刻。我们在来自五个多导睡眠图（PSG）队列（其中三个为临床队列，各队列均未纳入训练）的1,529个夜晚，以及224个头带夜晚上进行测试，并与GSSC、U-Sleep和YASA比较。【结果】在每小时0.5次假觉醒的匹配率下，WakeSentry在每个队列和两个头带上都比GSSC捕获更多觉醒。在PSG上，其敏感性从63.8%升至70.5%，平均高于U-Sleep和YASA。在头带上，其敏感性从49.8%升至53.9%，若无觉醒模块则该增益消失。使用在训练队列上预设的阈值时，它仍在七个测试集中的六个优于GSSC，每小时假觉醒最多为0.40次。作为回放的刺激器门控，它在五个测试集中缩短了清醒期刺激，同时在N2和N3期至少85%的时间内保持开放。【结论】因此，WakeSentry可在患者中以及未见过的头带上工作。它可在家庭环境中计数觉醒，并在每次觉醒时停止刺激，从而实现失眠的多夜监测，以及当睡眠者醒来时停止的闭环刺激。

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] In the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence (AI), statistics plays a crucial role in addressing challenges faced by medical AI. This review begins by highlighting the primary tasks of medical AI and the integration of statistical methodologies into their modeling processes. Despite the widespread application of AI in medicine and healthcare, key challenges persist: poor model interpretability, lack of causal reasoning, overfitting, unfairness, imbalanced datasets, AI "hallucinations" and "disinformation." Statistics provides unique strategies to tackle these challenges, including rigorous statistical design, regularization techniques, and statistical frameworks grounded in causal inference. Finally, the review offers several recommendations for the sustainable development of medical AI: enhancing data quality, promoting model simplicity and transparency, fostering independent validation standards, and facilitating interdisciplinary collaboration between statisticians and medical AI practitioners.

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Deep learning now underpins most protein-compound interaction (PCI) prediction pipelines, spanning virtual screening, affinity estimation, and lead optimization. Yet strong numbers on standard benchmarks do not reliably translate into discovery outcomes: accuracy can drop sharply under distribution shift, many predictions are hard to rationalize or corroborate with physical evidence, and reported performance is often sensitive to how labels are defined, how data are split, and which metrics are emphasized. In this review, we introduce recent progress in deep learning for PCI prediction across task definitions, protein/ligand representations, interaction modeling architectures, benchmark resources, and evaluation practice, emphasizing the methodological choices that determine reliability outside curated test sets. We relate widely used label and task setups to their underlying assumptions and typical failure modes, analyze how redundancy and similarity leakage can inflate in-distribution results, and highlight recurring trade-offs between model expressiveness, scalability, physical realism, and generalization to unseen targets or chemotypes. We end by outlining practical priorities for evaluation and reporting, including split protocols matched to the intended deployment scenario, explicit treatment of assay heterogeneity, uncertainty-aware and decision-focused metrics, and benchmark designs that better anticipate prospective utility.

abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits substantial biological and clinical heterogeneity, posing critical challenges for advancing precision medicine. Existing data-driven approaches often rely on modality-specific clustering or predefined biomarker trajectories, limiting their ability to discover disease subtypes from incomplete, heterogeneous real-world data. In this study, we introduce ADSMoE, a mixture-of-experts (MoE)-based multimodal representation learning framework that jointly identifies AD subtypes as latent disease signatures while accommodating incomplete modality combinations. ADSMoE integrates a Fleximodal MoE encoder that accommodates arbitrary combinations of available modalities with a novel subtype-specific MoE decoder to capture complementary disease characteristics through expert specialization. Using data from 5,422 participants across three independent cohorts, we trained ADSMoE on the ADNI cohort and externally validated the identified subtypes in NACC and UKB without model retraining. The proposed ADSMoE identified four AD subtypes with distinct neuroimaging patterns, genetic and proteomic associations, and clinical characteristics. Benchmarking analyses demonstrated robust subtype discovery and strong biological and clinical relevance, while external validation revealed consistent subtype-associated characteristics across independent cohorts. ADSMoE advances AD subtyping by uncovering biologically and clinically meaningful AD heterogeneity from incomplete multimodal data, providing a scalable framework for disease stratification, biomarker discovery, and future precision medicine applications in AD.

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Pulmonary diseases currently pose significant threats to global health, spanning common chronic conditions including lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and asthma, as well as infectious and inflammatory diseases like tuberculosis, interstitial lung disease (ILD), and COVID-19. Therefore, accurate diagnosis, effective therapeutic strategies, and reliable assessment of prognosis for pulmonary diseases are essential for improving patient outcomes and safeguarding public health. Despite the increasing availability of medical imaging and pathological data owing to improvements in detection technologies, what is becoming increasingly evident are the limitations of conventional diagnosis, which relies solely on clinicians' subjective judgment based on imaging, pulmonary function, pathology, and clinical experience. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) technology, especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has made significant progress in areas such as image recognition and model construction. Numerous studies have demonstrated the widespread application of AI in the screening and diagnosis of lung diseases, the optimization of treatment strategies, and prognosis assessment, revealing its remarkable ability to process and interpret complex clinical data. Although concerns persist regarding data quality, the "black box" nature of algorithms, clinical practice, and the regulatory landscape, the application of AI in lung disease research and clinical care is more and more promising. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of AI in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary diseases, analyze the challenges and limitations of current AI technologies ranging from data and algorithms to clinical translation, and highlight directions for future research.

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] The inherent complexity and heterogeneity of cancer create an urgent need for individualized treatment strategies. However, traditional population-based medical approaches have limitations in addressing patient-specific differences. Meanwhile, conventional clinical trials are often constrained by lengthy timelines, high costs, and difficulties in patient recruitment, particularly for rare cancers and pediatric populations, thereby hindering the development of novel therapies. To address these challenges, medical digital twins (MDTs) have emerged as dynamic computational models that represent an individual patient's physiology and disease state and are continuously updated as real-world data accumulate. To explain how MDTs transform accumulating patient data into actionable insights, this chapter first introduces their fundamental architecture, comprising five interdependent components: the patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and twin synchronization. Within this architecture, the patient-in-silico component can be constructed using mechanistic models based on established biological principles, artificial intelligence models driven by large-scale clinical data, or hybrid models combining both approaches. Representative mechanistic and artificial intelligence-driven MDTs are then presented to illustrate how these modeling approaches have been applied in oncology. Specifically, MDTs can support precision oncology and improve the efficiency of clinical trials. In precision oncology, MDTs can simulate disease progression and therapeutic responses, allowing treatment regimens to be tested virtually before administration and thereby supporting personalized treatment decisions. In virtual clinical trials, MDTs can enhance randomized trials through the PROCOVA™ methodology, provide synthetic control arms for single-arm studies, and support the identification of optimal dosing regimens in early-phase trials. However, MDTs also face challenges related to computational complexity, generalizability across diverse populations, AI-related model validation and regulatory compliance, and underdeveloped ethical frameworks for continuous-learning systems. Despite these challenges, MDTs hold considerable potential to reshape cancer care, optimize individualized therapies, and accelerate oncology drug development.

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] The rapid growth of electronic health records, clinical trial repositories, and real-world medical data creates new opportunities for estimating how treatment effects vary across patients. abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been instrumental in uncovering the genetic basis of complex traits, yet classical single-variant testing remains limited in power and biological interpretability. This chapter reviews the evolving methodological landscape of AI-enabled GWAS, highlights key advances in variant discovery and functional interpretation, and discusses remaining challenges such as ancestry bias, interpretability, and the need for biological validation. abstract: [Biomedicine & pharmacotherapy = Biomedecine & pharmacotherapie] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in cardiovascular research where conventional analysis struggles with scale, heterogeneity, and multimodal integration. Its contribution differs across imaging, computational omics, mechanistic simulation, and drug discovery. This narrative review examines substantive applications of machine learning and deep learning while distinguishing them from routine bioinformatics and purely biophysical modeling. We assess independent biological units, validation strategies, and strength of inference in representative studies. Deep-learning imaging systems can provide reproducible quantitative phenotypes, but workflow performance alone does not establish mechanism. In single-cell and spatial studies, clustering, integration, trajectory inference, and network reconstruction generally yield associations or hypotheses unless experimentally supported. Mechanistic interpretation is bounded by the specific effect established through targeted perturbation or rescue with functional testing; lineage tracing and orthogonal readouts provide complementary support, not standalone proof of causation. Hybrid AI-biophysical models may accelerate personalized simulation, whereas heart-on-chip, engineered tissue, and organoid systems without learned components are validation platforms rather than AI methods. In drug discovery, active learning and molecular redesign can prioritize candidates, but predicted reductions in ion-channel liability do not demonstrate biological safety or reduced proarrhythmic risk. Major limitations include pseudoreplication, data leakage, domain shift, batch effects, uncertain labels, few independent hearts, demographic imbalance, incomplete calibration, and limited transfer among animal, iPSC-derived, and adult human systems. AI is most valuable when it produces robust phenotypes or experimentally testable hypotheses within a transparent validation framework, rather than when predictive accuracy is treated as mechanistic evidence.

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is difficult to identify rapidly because clinical symptoms may be delayed and conventional CT or MRI often reveals no structural abnormalities. Biomechanics-based monitoring provides an objective complementary strategy by measuring head kinematics at the moment of impact and estimating the resulting brain deformation. This review summarizes how artificial intelligence (AI) can overcome two major barriers to this approach: errors in wearable-sensor measurements and the high computational cost of finite element head models. AI-based methods can denoise instrumented mouthguard signals, distinguish true impacts from false triggers, and infer impact direction, location, speed, and force. Deep learning head models can further map six-degree-of-freedom head kinematics to whole-brain strain and strain-rate distributions within milliseconds, enabling near-real-time tissue-level injury assessment. Recent advances, including kinematic feature optimization, principal component analysis, impact subtyping, transfer learning, unsupervised domain adaptation, and spatiotemporal prediction, have improved model efficiency, interpretability, and generalizability across impact scenarios. Integrating wearable sensing with AI-accelerated brain modeling could support rapid removal from exposure, earlier clinical evaluation and intervention, and monitoring of cumulative impact dose. Future research should improve sensor wearability and coupling, incorporate subject-specific brain morphology and cortical folding, represent cerebrospinal fluid mechanics more realistically, and develop unified models that jointly estimate brain deformation and predict clinically confirmed injury. AI-enabled biomechanical monitoring may therefore complement symptom- and imaging-based assessments and advance real-time, personalized mTBI detection and prevention.
zh_abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] 轻度创伤性脑损伤（mTBI）难以快速识别，因为临床症状可能延迟出现，且常规 CT 或 MRI 常无结构异常。基于生物力学的监测通过测量撞击瞬间的头部运动学并估计由此产生的脑变形，提供了一种客观的补充策略。本综述总结了人工智能（AI）如何克服该方法的两大障碍：可穿戴传感器测量误差和有限元头部模型的高计算成本。基于 AI 的方法可对仪器化护齿信号去噪，区分真实撞击与假触发，并推断撞击方向、位置、速度和力。深度学习头部模型可进一步在数毫秒内将六自由度头部运动学映射为全脑应变和应变率分布，从而实现近实时的组织水平损伤评估。近期进展，包括运动学特征优化、主成分分析、撞击亚型划分、迁移学习、无监督域适应和时空预测，提高了模型效率、可解释性以及在各种撞击情景中的泛化能力。将可穿戴传感与 AI 加速的脑建模相结合，可支持快速脱离暴露、更早的临床评估和干预，以及累积撞击剂量监测。未来研究应改善传感器的可佩戴性和耦合，纳入受试者特异性脑形态和皮层折叠，更真实地表示脑脊液力学，并开发联合估计脑变形和预测临床确诊损伤的统一模型。因此，AI 赋能的生物力学监测可补充基于症状和影像的评估，并推进实时、个性化的 mTBI 检测和预防。

abstract: [Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM] The complex structures and dynamic processes of lipids make it challenging to decipher lipid reprogramming in metabolic diseases. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with lipidomics, mass spectrometry imaging, and lipid metabolic fluxomics enables rapid, high-precision, and in-depth spatiotemporal profiling of lipid species. In this review, we summarize advances in AI-empowered lipidomics, which not only accelerate spatiotemporal data processing but also offer new avenues to resolve the heterogeneity of lipid metabolism. Importantly, AI-assisted lipidomics could identify candidate biomarkers and generate testable hypotheses about disease mechanisms. Furthermore, we evaluate whether computational advances yield trustworthy evidence by examining annotation confidence, quantitative accuracy, cross-platform reproducibility, uncertainty calibration, and external validation. We also address the current limitations of AI-assisted lipidomics, particularly the risk of AI hallucinations.
zh_abstract: [Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM] 脂质的复杂结构和动态过程使得解析代谢疾病中的脂质重编程具有挑战性。将人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI）与脂质组学、质谱成像和脂质代谢通量组学相结合，能够对脂质种类进行快速、高精度且深入的时空分析。在本综述中，我们总结了人工智能赋能脂质组学的进展，这些进展不仅加速了时空数据处理，还为解析脂质代谢异质性提供了新途径。重要的是，人工智能辅助脂质组学能够识别候选生物标志物，并就疾病机制提出可检验的假设。此外，我们通过考察注释置信度、定量准确性、跨平台可重复性、不确定性校准和外部验证，评估计算进展是否能产生可信证据。我们还讨论了人工智能辅助脂质组学当前的局限性，尤其是人工智能幻觉的风险。

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Human-Virus Protein-Protein Interactions (HV-PPIs) are the core mechanisms underlying viral invasion of host cells, completion of the viral life cycle, and induction of pathological responses. Predicting HV-PPIs in higher accuracy is of great significance for elucidating viral pathogenic mechanisms, developing antiviral drugs, and designing vaccines. However, traditional experimental methods such as Yeast Two-Hybrid (Y2H) and Affinity Purification-Mass Spectrometry (AP-MS) face bottlenecks including low throughput, high cost, high false positive rates, and incomplete data in the identification of cross-species interactions. In recent years, computational biology approaches, especially deep learning-based multimodal fusion frameworks, have emerged as the primary driving force for accelerating HV-PPIs prediction. This review systematically summarizes the latest advances in the field of HV-PPIs prediction, elaborates on key aspects such as data construction, feature engineering, deep learning architectures, and performance evaluation, summarizes the technical essentials, advantages, and limitations of existing methods, discusses the development trends of the field by integrating representative research findings from recent years, and serves as a reference for future investigations in this domain.
zh_abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] 人-病毒蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（Human-Virus Protein-Protein Interactions, HV-PPIs）是病毒侵入宿主细胞、完成病毒生命周期并诱导病理反应的核心机制。以更高准确性预测 HV-PPIs 对于阐明病毒致病机制、开发抗病毒药物和设计疫苗具有重要意义。然而，酵母双杂交（Yeast Two-Hybrid, Y2H）和亲和纯化-质谱（Affinity Purification-Mass Spectrometry, AP-MS）等传统实验方法在鉴定跨物种相互作用时面临通量低、成本高、假阳性率高和数据不完整等瓶颈。近年来，计算生物学方法，尤其是基于深度学习的多模态融合框架，已成为加速 HV-PPIs 预测的主要驱动力。本综述系统总结了 HV-PPIs 预测领域的最新进展，阐述了数据构建、特征工程、深度学习架构和性能评估等关键方面，概括了现有方法的技术要点、优势和局限性，结合近年代表性研究成果讨论了该领域的发展趋势，并为该领域未来研究提供参考。

abstract: [Current opinion in ophthalmology] This review examines the current state of artificial intelligence (AI) models for the detection and prediction of glaucomatous progression. Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed to analyze longitudinal data from optic disc photographs, optical coherence tomography images, and visual field tests to identify worsening glaucoma. Recent AI research has also expanded beyond simply detecting progression to predicting future disease trajectories. These approaches may provide more efficient assessment than clinician review alone. AI models can rapidly analyze large volumes of clinical data to support individualized glaucoma management; these models can guide treatment intensity and follow-up intervals by detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression. However, significant hurdles to clinical adoption remain, including the "black box" nature of AI, absence of a universally accepted reference standard for progression, variable data quality, and limited generalizability across populations and clinical settings. AI is poised to function as a clinical decision support tool rather than a replacement for clinicians. Prospective studies are needed to determine the impact of AI in improving patient outcomes, clinical efficiency, and healthcare costs.
zh_abstract: 【当前眼科学观点】本综述考察了用于检测和预测青光眼性进展的人工智能（AI）模型的现状。已开发出机器学习和深度学习模型，用于分析来自视盘照片、光学相干断层扫描图像和视野检查的纵向数据，以识别青光眼的恶化。近期 AI 研究也已超出单纯检测进展的范围，扩展到预测未来的疾病轨迹。这些方法可能比仅靠临床医师审阅提供更高效的评估。AI 模型能够快速分析大量临床数据，以支持个体化青光眼管理；这些模型可通过检测和预测青光眼性进展来指导治疗强度和随访间隔。然而，临床采用仍存在重大障碍，包括 AI 的“黑箱”性质、缺乏普遍接受的进展参考标准、数据质量参差不齐，以及在人群和临床环境之间泛化能力有限。AI 有望作为临床决策支持工具发挥作用，而非取代临床医师。尚需前瞻性研究来确定 AI 在改善患者结局、临床效率和医疗成本方面的影响。

zh_abstract: 准确的癌症诊断依赖于组织病理学评估，其中肿瘤形态驱动疾病分类和治疗决策。尽管深度学习模型在从组织病理学图像预测诊断和预后特性方面已表现出强大性能，但其临床采用仍因缺乏可解释性而受限。与传统医学图像中诊断发现具有空间定位不同，组织病理学图像的特征是分布在整个全切片图像（WSI）中的复杂纹理模式，这使得仅通过基于区域的定位来解释模型预测变得困难。反事实解释提供了一种有前景的替代方法，其追问“图像中哪些变化本可能改变模型预测”。为实现这一点，我们提出SCALE，一个用于生成此类反事实解释的框架。

title: An LLM-assisted Pipeline for Identifying ClinicalTrials.gov Registry Changes and Their Association with Primary Endpoint Positivity

abstract: Registration of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in a public registry such as ClinicalTrials.gov should minimize the risk of reporting bias. However, records may be modified during a trial and the resulting discrepancies are not always apparent without a detailed examination of all version histories, a process that is cumbersome when performed manually. We developed an automated workflow to investigate whether specific changes to RCT registry entries are associated with primary endpoint positivity. Our pipeline extracts RCT records from ClinicalTrials.gov and systematically detects changes between successive versions using a combination of deterministic textual analysis and large language model (LLM)-assisted classification. We could show a positive association between trial positivity and changes to primary outcomes (OR 1.91; 95% CI 1.48-2.47) as well as to arms and interventions (OR 2.10; 95% CI 1.62-2.73). Associations were weaker when changes occurred exclusively before the primary completion date, pointing to the importance of timing in evaluating potentially consequential modifications to RCT design. Our automated pipeline can enable analysis of trial registration records at scale, facilitating the work of reviewers and meta-scientists to promote research integrity.
zh_abstract: 在ClinicalTrials.gov等公共注册平台注册随机临床试验（RCT）应能最大限度降低报告偏倚风险。然而，试验期间记录可能被修改，若不详细检查所有版本历史，由此产生的差异并不总是显而易见；人工执行这一过程十分繁琐。我们开发了一套自动化工作流程，以研究RCT注册条目中的特定更改是否与主要终点阳性相关。我们的流程从ClinicalTrials.gov提取RCT记录，并结合确定性文本分析和大型语言模型（LLM）辅助分类，系统检测连续版本之间的变化。我们能够显示，试验阳性与主要结局的更改（OR 1.91；95% CI 1.48-2.47）以及研究组和干预措施的更改（OR 2.10；95% CI 1.62-2.73）之间存在正相关。当更改仅发生在主要完成日期之前时，相关性较弱，这指出在评估RCT设计中可能具有重要影响的修改时，时机的重要性。我们的自动化流程能够实现大规模分析试验注册记录，促进审稿人和元科学家的工作，以提升研究诚信。

title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding

summary: 综述临床大模型幻觉、智能体幻觉级联、过程奖励建模与神经符号约束四条可验证推理路径。

abstract: Clinical large language models are usually judged by whether the final answer is right. Yet a model can reach a fluent, plausible output through invalid reasoning that static benchmarks do not detect, and confident hallucination, causally invalid inference, and spurious demographic shortcuts can pass conventional evaluation. This critical review covers four paradigms in turn: how clinical hallucination arises and why static metrics miss it; the agentic hallucination cascade, in which multi-agent and tool-augmented systems propagate and amplify early reasoning errors; process reward modeling as step-level supervision; and neuro-symbolic grounding, in which formal logic engines, ontology reasoners, and knowledge graphs place verifiable constraints on neural output. Within their encoded domains, systems with symbolic veto layers offer guarantees that hold relative to their encoded knowledge

abstract: Vision transformers tokenize an image into patches, which couples the token count to resolution and requires the embedding to be learned from data. This approach defines each token as one spectral mode, and the sequence length is chosen rather than implied by resolution, reducing the cost of attention. abstract: Pretraining filtering is one of the most common safeguards for open-weight language models. Here we study its effectiveness, durability and scalability using the ESM-2 family of protein language models. We find that filtering viral proteins from the pretraining data meaningfully degrades masked language modelling, mutation effect prediction and long-range contact prediction on viral proteins, while largely preserving performance on non-viral proteins. These effects are concentrated among proteins from human-infecting viruses, and grow as we scale models from 8M to 3B parameters. As models increase in size, we find that stringent filtering becomes more effective. However, fine-tuning on sequences from the removed viral families restores the lost performance. Although the cost to recover performance increases with model scale, even for the largest models it costs about 80 USD of H100 time.

abstract: Reconstructing cellular dynamics from snapshots is challenging because the destructive nature of single-cell measurements makes tracking the same cells over time impossible. Cellular dynamics are inherently stochastic and involve changes in population size through proliferation and apoptosis. Growth-based methods represent population change as a rate on the density, which does not assign exits and entries to individual cells. Unbalanced Schrödinger bridges model individual events, but neural solvers for killed diffusion bridges simulate trajectories during training. abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Precision medicine, which involves tailoring medical treatment to the individual characteristics of each patient, is poised for a new era of advancement through artificial intelligence (AI). abstract: Motivation: Pathogen phylogenies are useful for monitoring the evolution of pathogens and for detecting new variants, as it provides information that can aid public health decisions and outbreak response. Since not all infections are sequenced, certain pathogen lineages may be missing or only poorly represented in reconstructed phylogenies. Identifying these gaps could help to determine where additional data collection is required. Results: We developed a computational method to locate regions of missing samples from the observed tree alone, without sequences from those samples. A machine learning model predicts which branches lead toward the missing region. Beam search then identifies three representative paths and estimates a candidate most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of the missing region for each path. We tested this framework on 5,000 simulated phylogenies where we controlled which tips were deleted. On an independent test set, the best candidate recovered an average of 89.9% of deleted tips, increasing to 90.7% when all three candidates were combined. Predicted and true MRCAs lay on the same ancestral-descendant lineage in 91.3% of cases. We further evaluated the approach on an empirical SARS-CoV-2 phylogeny with introduced missingness. By identifying potentially underrepresented lineages, this framework could help real-time identification of missing infections and improve outbreak response.

Midwives play a crucial role in identifying these risks, providing preventive counseling, and promoting climate-resilient perinatal care. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI)-supported simulation into midwifery education may enhance students' knowledge, climate change awareness, and clinical risk assessment skills. This study aims to evaluate the effect of climate-resilient perinatal care training supported by an AI-powered chatbot simulator on midwifery students' climate change knowledge, awareness, and climate-related perinatal risk assessment skills. The study is designed as a randomized controlled trial with pretest, posttest, and four-week follow-up assessments. A total of 88 third- and fourth-year midwifery students at the University of Health Sciences, Hamidiye Faculty of Health Sciences, Türkiye, will be allocated to an intervention group (n=44) or a control group (n=44) using stratified randomization based on academic year and grade point average. Both groups will receive a four-week climate-resilient perinatal care education program consisting of eight hours of face-to-face training. Following the educational program, the intervention group will participate in AI-powered chatbot-based clinical simulations involving climate-related perinatal health scenarios, while the control group will receive an educational brochure. Climate-resilient perinatal care knowledge and climate change awareness will be assessed in both groups at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at a four-week follow-up. Climate-related perinatal risk assessment skills will additionally be evaluated in the intervention group at posttest and follow-up using a structured observational assessment tool. The findings are expected to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of AI-supported simulation in climate-resilient midwifery education.
zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：Büşra HIZLIOL；研究条件：气候韧性围产期护理教育；类型：INTERVENTIONAL；阶段：NA；入组人数：88；状态：NOT_YET_RECRUITING] 气候变化通过极端高温、空气污染和气候相关灾害等环境危害，对孕产妇、胎儿和新生儿健康构成重大风险。助产士在识别这些风险、提供预防性咨询和促进气候韧性围产期护理方面发挥关键作用。将人工智能（AI）支持的模拟整合到助产教育中，可能增强学生的知识、气候变化意识和临床风险评估技能。本研究旨在评估由AI驱动的聊天机器人模拟器支持的气候韧性围产期护理培训对助产专业学生气候变化知识、意识和气候相关围产期风险评估技能的影响。该研究设计为随机对照试验，包含前测、后测和四周随访评估。土耳其健康科学大学Hamidiye健康科学学院的88名三年级和四年级助产专业学生将根据学年和平均绩点采用分层随机化，分配到干预组（n=44）或对照组（n=44）。两组都将接受为期四周、包含八小时面授培训的气候韧性围产期护理教育项目。教育项目结束后，干预组将参加基于AI驱动聊天机器人的临床模拟，涉及气候相关围产期健康情景，而对照组将收到教育手册。将在基线、干预后立即和四周随访时评估两组的气候韧性围产期护理知识和气候变化意识。还将使用结构化观察评估工具，在干预组后测和随访时评估气候相关围产期风险评估技能。研究结果预计将为AI支持模拟在气候韧性助产教育中的有效性提供证据。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Yalin Aygun; conditions: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD); type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 750; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] ADHD is one of the most common mental health conditions in teenagers. It can affect school performance, friendships, and overall well-being. Some everyday habits and lifestyle factors-how much a teenager plays internet games, how well they sleep, and whether they take part in sports-have each been linked to ADHD symptoms. However, these three factors have almost always been studied one at a time, and no study has yet tested whether looking at them together can help predict which teenagers have more severe ADHD symptoms. This study aims to find out whether internet gaming, sleep quality, and sport participation, when considered together, can predict ADHD symptom severity in adolescents aged 12-17. We will invite 750 teenagers from secondary schools in Malatya, Türkiye, to complete a set of short, anonymous questionnaires about their attention and hyperactivity symptoms, gaming habits, sleep, and sport participation. We will then use machine learning-a type of computer analysis that can detect complex patterns and interactions between many factors at once-to build and test a prediction model. The main question this study seeks to answer is: Do internet gaming, sleep quality, and sport participation jointly carry information that helps predict ADHD symptoms in teenagers, beyond what is already known from basic characteristics such as age, sex, and socioeconomic status? We are not testing a treatment, and the study does not involve any medication, biological samples, or changes to participants' usual routines. The findings may help schools, families, and health professionals identify teenagers who could benefit from early support and from healthier lifestyle habits. This is an exploratory study; it cannot show cause and effect, and any prediction model would need to be tested in other groups before being used in practice.
zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：Yalin Aygun；疾病：注意缺陷/多动障碍（ADHD）；类型：观察性；入组人数：750；状态：尚未招募] ADHD是青少年中最常见的心理健康状况之一。它可能影响学业表现、友谊和整体福祉。一些日常习惯和生活方式因素——青少年玩网络游戏的程度、睡眠质量如何，以及是否参加体育运动——各自都与ADHD症状相关。然而，这三个因素几乎总是被逐一研究，尚无研究检验将它们放在一起是否有助于预测哪些青少年有更严重的ADHD症状。本研究旨在查明，将网络游戏、睡眠质量和体育参与共同考虑时，是否能预测12-17岁青少年的ADHD症状严重程度。我们将邀请土耳其马拉蒂亚中学的750名青少年完成一组简短、匿名的问卷，内容涉及他们的注意和多动症状、游戏习惯、睡眠和体育参与。然后，我们将使用机器学习——一种能够同时检测许多因素之间复杂模式和相互作用的计算机分析——来构建并测试一个预测模型。本研究试图回答的主要问题是：网络游戏、睡眠质量和体育参与共同是否携带有助于预测青少年ADHD症状的信息，且超出年龄、性别和社会经济状况等基本特征已知的信息？我们不是在测试一种治疗，研究不涉及任何药物、生物样本或对参与者日常作息改变。研究结果可能有助于学校、家庭和卫生专业人员识别可从早期支持和更健康生活方式习惯中获益的青少年。这是一项探索性研究；它不能显示因果关系，任何预测模型在用于实践前都需要在其他群体中测试。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Istinye University; conditions: Post-Spinal Hypotension; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 250; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This study aims to develop and prospectively validate machine learning models for predicting hypotension following spinal anesthesia in pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean delivery. The study consists of two cohorts: a retrospective training cohort including at least 200 patients and an independent prospective validation cohort including 50 patients. Three machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression) will be trained using preoperative demographic, anthropometric, and baseline hemodynamic variables, including age, body mass index, parity, gestational age, baseline systolic blood pressure, and baseline heart rate. The primary outcome is post-spinal hypotension, defined as a decrease in systolic blood pressure of at least 20% from baseline and/or the requirement for vasopressor administration within the first 15 minutes after spinal anesthesia. The best-performing model will be evaluated in the independent prospective cohort to assess its predictive performance in a real clinical setting.

abstract: [Heart failure clinics] Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for improving diagnosis and prognostic assessment across a wide spectrum of cardiovascular diseases. A literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase to identify relevant studies focusing on ML approaches to computed tomography (CT)-based risk stratification in aortic dissection. ML-based analysis of CT imaging offers significant potential to enhance prognostic assessment and risk stratification in aortic dissection. By integrating imaging, clinical, and biomarker data, these approaches may enable earlier identification of high-risk patients and support more personalized management strategies.
